verdict.summary: You create a Notion public connection in the Developer portal and get an OAuth client ID and secret right away. As far as the docs say, OAuth for any workspace needs no review. Only the optional Marketplace listing is reviewed. The one decision you can't undo is the installation scope ('Any workspace' or 'Selected workspaces only'), because it can't be changed after creation.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 20-40 min (plus 1-3 hours if you also prepare a Marketplace listing)
verdict.approval_wait: none for OAuth; 5-10 business days only if you want a Marketplace listing

gates.name: Public connection in your development workspace
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Notion workspace through your own OAuth client (for example, via a Composio auth config) as soon as the connection exists.
limits: You need a workspace where you are owner/admin. A free personal workspace works.
Only pages you pick in the consent page picker are shared.

gates.name: Installation scope: Selected workspaces only
gates.unlocks: Users in the workspaces you selected can each run the OAuth flow and connect. Notion has no separate test-user allowlist; this installation scope is how you restrict who can install.
limits: Installs are limited to the selected workspaces.
Installation scope can't be changed later. To switch to 'Any workspace' you must create a new connection, which means a new client ID and secret, so users must re-authorize.
Each user must authorize individually and only sees pages they have full access to.
Rate limit per connection: 180 requests/min, or 600 requests/min on Business/Enterprise workspaces.

gates.name: Installation scope: Any workspace (Marketplace listing optional)
gates.unlocks: Any Notion user in any workspace can authorize your connection. The docs describe no review before public OAuth use. A Marketplace listing is a separate, optional step that is reviewed.
limits: Marketplace listing review typically takes 5-10 business days, with the reply by email.
Only 'Any workspace' connections can be listed.
One docs screenshot caption says the Authorization URL field fills in only after submission for review. This conflicts with the rest of the docs, so check it in your console.
gates.time_to_reach: Immediately for OAuth; 5-10 business days for a Marketplace listing

steps.title: Get a Notion workspace you own
steps.detail: Sign in to Notion with an account that is owner/admin of a workspace. If you aren't an admin anywhere, create a free personal workspace and use it as your development workspace.
gotchas: The docs state the owner requirement for internal connections. It is unclear whether it also applies to public connections, so use an owned workspace to be safe.

steps.title: Open the Developer portal and start a public connection
steps.detail: Go to the Developer portal. In the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections, then click Create new connection.
gotchas: The portal is a JavaScript app and requires you to be signed in to Notion.

steps.title: Choose installation scope (permanent)
steps.detail: Pick 'Any workspace' if you want anyone to connect or plan a Marketplace listing. Pick 'Selected workspaces only' to restrict installs to specific workspaces. You can't change this later.
gotchas: Switching later means a new connection with new credentials, and every user has to re-authorize.
For a product used by external customers, 'Any workspace' is almost always the right choice.

steps.title: Fill in name, workspace, redirect URI and capabilities
steps.detail: Enter the connection name and select your development workspace. Add the redirect URI, then set capabilities: Read, Update and Insert content, plus a user-information level. Request only what your agent needs; 'User information with email addresses' is the most sensitive.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Capabilities
values.value: Read content, Update content, Insert content (as needed)

values.label: User information
values.value: No user information / without email / with email (choose the minimum)

gotchas: Add only one redirect URI. With more than one, redirect_uri becomes required at token exchange.
Notion has no scope strings. Access comes from capabilities plus the pages each user selects.

steps.title: Copy the OAuth client ID and secret
steps.detail: After creating the connection, open the Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret. Store the secret in a secrets manager.
gotchas: The docs say the Authorization URL field may stay empty until the connection is submitted for review. That doesn't block you, because Composio builds the authorize URL from the client ID.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for the notion toolkit using OAuth2 with your own client ID and secret instead of the managed app. Leave scopes empty. Confirm the callback URL shown matches the redirect URI you entered in Notion.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection. The authorize URL should go to https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and owner=user. In the page picker, select the pages to share, then confirm that a token is issued and an API call returns data from those pages.
gotchas: If the consent prompt is cancelled, Notion redirects with error=access_denied.
The API can only see pages the user selected. If a page is missing, the user needs to re-run consent and select it.

steps.title: Confirm refresh token rotation is handled
steps.detail: Each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token, so always save the newest refresh token. Composio manages this for connected accounts. If you store tokens yourself, verify that you persist the rotated refresh token.

steps.title: Plan for rate limits
steps.detail: Each connection gets 180 requests/min, or 600 requests/min when the user's workspace is on Business or Enterprise, counted over a fixed 60-second window. Back off on HTTP 429 using Retry-After. Don't retry when rate_limit_reason is public_api_request_blocked.

steps.title: (Optional) Draft a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Prepare a name, description, category, tags, listing images and a logo for your 'Any workspace' connection. Check for brand/trademark problems, such as using 'Notion' in your name or logo, which are a common reason for rejection.

steps.title: (Optional) Submit the listing for review
steps.detail: In the Developer portal, go to Listings > Connections > Start a new connection listing. Link your public connection, enter the listing content and submit it for review by the Notion team.

steps.title: (Optional) Wait for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Notion typically replies by email within 5-10 business days. If the listing is rejected, fix the stated issues and resubmit. Your OAuth connection keeps working for users the whole time.

requirements.item: A Notion workspace where you are owner/admin
requirements.detail: Needed to create a connection. A free personal workspace is acceptable.

requirements.item: Connection name, development workspace, redirect URI, installation scope and capabilities
requirements.detail: All are required when creating a public connection.
Required for anyone outside the selected workspaces to install, and for a Marketplace listing. Set once, at creation.
Name, description, category, tags, listing images, logo and the linked public connection. Needed only for a Marketplace listing.

scopes.scope: Read content / Update content / Insert content (capabilities)
scopes.effect: Set on the connection; Notion has no OAuth scope strings. Each user also limits access by choosing pages at consent. No review is tied to these capabilities.
Adds user email addresses to User objects. It is the most sensitive user-info level, so request it only if needed. The docs describe no extra review for it.

blockers.symptom: You need to let any workspace install, or list on the Marketplace, but the connection was created as 'Selected workspaces only'.
blockers.cause: Installation scope is set at creation and can't be changed.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with 'Any workspace', update the client ID and secret in Composio, and have users re-authorize.

blockers.symptom: The Authorization URL field in the Configuration tab is empty.
blockers.cause: A docs caption says this field fills in only after the connection is submitted for review.
blockers.fix: Build the authorize URL from the client ID (Composio does this). If authorization actually fails before review, submit the connection for review.

blockers.symptom: The API returns 404 or empty results for pages the user expects to see.
blockers.cause: Only pages the user selected in the consent page picker are shared, and the picker shows only pages the user has full access to.
blockers.fix: Have the user re-run the connection flow and select the missing pages.

blockers.cause: Notion has restricted the connection's API access; retrying won't help.
blockers.fix: Stop retrying and contact Notion support about the restriction.

blockers.cause: Brand/trademark issues, quality concerns, or not meeting the baseline connection criteria.
blockers.fix: Fix the issues named in the rejection email and resubmit.

composio.note: Composio's managed Notion OAuth app is fine for prototyping. Notion has no scope strings, so access depends on the connection's capabilities and the pages each user shares. Register your own public connection when you want your app name on the consent screen, different capabilities (for example, user emails), your own per-connection rate-limit budget, or a Marketplace listing. Creating one needs no review before OAuth works. An API_KEY mode (internal connection token or personal access token) also exists for single-workspace use.

evidence.claim: Composio offers managed OAuth2 for Notion with no default scopes; authorize/token URLs are api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize and /token; an API_KEY mode exists.
evidence.quote: "managed_oauth_available": true ... "default_scopes": []

evidence.claim: Notion has internal connections, personal access tokens, and OAuth 2.0 public connections.
evidence.quote: Internal connections use a static credential called an internal connection API token, personal access tokens use a user-scoped static token, and public connections use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

evidence.claim: Public connections are created via Build > Public connections > Create new connection in the Developer portal.
evidence.quote: In the **Build** section of the sidebar, select **Public connections**.

evidence.claim: Required fields: connection name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope, capabilities.
evidence.quote: Connection name and development workspace

evidence.claim: Installation scope ('Any workspace' or 'Selected workspaces only') is set at creation and can't be changed.
evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.

evidence.claim: The Configuration tab shows the OAuth client ID and secret after creation.
evidence.quote: After creation, visit the **Configuration** tab to retrieve your **OAuth client ID** and **OAuth client secret**.

evidence.claim: You must be a workspace owner to create a connection (stated for internal connections).
evidence.quote: You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection.

evidence.claim: A free personal workspace can be created if you aren't an admin anywhere.
evidence.quote: If you're not an admin in any of your workspaces, you can create a personal workspace for free.

evidence.claim: Authorize URL requires client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, owner=user; state is optional; no PKCE parameters are listed.
evidence.quote: The URL begins with `https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize`

evidence.claim: Token exchange uses Basic auth; redirect_uri is required with multiple redirect URIs, otherwise not allowed (unless passed on the authorize URL).
evidence.quote: If there are more than one redirect URIs included in your connection settings, this field is required. Otherwise, it is not allowed.

evidence.claim: Refreshing returns a new access token and a new refresh token (rotation).
evidence.quote: Refreshing an access token will generate a new access token and a new refresh token.

evidence.claim: A screenshot caption says the Authorization URL field fills in only after submission for review; this may be outdated.
evidence.quote: The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review

evidence.claim: Access is controlled by capabilities, not OAuth scope strings, plus the pages users pick at consent.
evidence.quote: All connections and personal access tokens have associated capabilities which enforce what they can do and see in a Notion workspace.

evidence.claim: The 'User information with email addresses' level exposes user emails.
evidence.quote: User information with email addresses: Selecting this option ensures that User objects will include all information about the user, including name, profile image, and their email address.

evidence.claim: Each user authorizes individually and shares only the pages they pick.
evidence.quote: each prospective user needs to individually follow the auth flow for the connection.

evidence.claim: A Marketplace listing is optional; public connections work without one.
evidence.quote: Public connections work independently of Marketplace listings.

evidence.claim: Marketplace listings are created under Listings > Connections and submitted for Notion team review.
evidence.quote: Submit your listing for review by the Notion team.

evidence.claim: Marketplace review typically replies within 5-10 business days.
evidence.quote: expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.

evidence.claim: Rejection reasons include brand/trademark issues, quality concerns, and unmet baseline criteria.
evidence.quote: Connections are rejected for various reasons, from brand/trademark issues to quality concerns to situations where the baseline connection criteria isn't met.

evidence.claim: Only 'Any workspace' connections can be listed on the Marketplace.
evidence.quote: Only public connections with an installation scope of **Any workspace** can be listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Per-connection rate limits are 600 req/min (Business/Enterprise) or 180 req/min (other plans), with 429 and Retry-After; no install caps are mentioned.
evidence.quote: All other plans | 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second)

evidence.claim: rate_limit_reason public_api_request_blocked marks restricted connections, where retrying won't help.
evidence.quote: 600 requests per minute on Business and Enterprise, 180 requests per minute on every other plan

evidence.claim: The Developer portal URL loads as a JavaScript app shell; sign-in is needed in practice.
evidence.quote: JavaScript must be enabled in order to use Notion.

evidence.claim: A cancelled consent redirects with error=access_denied.
evidence.quote: www.example.com/my-redirect-uri?error=access_denied&state=

evidence.claim: There is no app-level review before a public connection's OAuth works; review applies only to the optional Marketplace listing (f12 hints otherwise).
